## 1. Open Studio on the Projects pillar

The Projects pillar lists every project forge manages.

![Open Studio on the Projects pillar](/media/stories/proof/01-open-studio-on-the-projects-pillar.png)

## 2. Click the card for a project this repository carries

The card is a real link to that project’s own page — the route is the project the previous beat found, not one written down in advance.

![Click the card for a project this repository carries](/media/stories/proof/02-click-the-card-for-a-project-this-reposi.png)

## 3. Go back to the Projects pillar

The Projects pillar is one click away from anywhere in Studio.

![Go back to the Projects pillar](/media/stories/proof/03-go-back-to-the-projects-pillar.png)

## 4. Click "Onboard a project"

Onboarding asks for the few things a Factory needs before it can build a repo: what to call it, the quality gate that judges its work, and the north star that tells a planner what it is for.

![Click "Onboard a project"](/media/stories/proof/04-click-onboard-a-project.png)

## 5. Fill in the name, the quality gate and the north star — and under Advanced, the repo path — then press "Onboard project →"

Registering the project lands the operator on its page.

![Fill in the name, the quality gate and the north star — and under Advanced, the repo path — then press "Onboard project →"](/media/stories/proof/05-fill-in-the-name-the-quality-gate-and-th.png)
